meetingTitle: FinCorp Global - Enterprise Solution Discovery & Security Review
executiveSummary: FinCorp Global is evaluating OmniNote AI to automate meeting transcription, compliance audit trails, and executive note distribution for 1,200 financial analysts. Arthur Pendelton's core concerns centered around SOC 2 Type II attestation, data residency in Frankfurt/Zurich, and zero data retention for AI model training. Liam confirmed private tenant isolation and customer-managed KMS encryption keys.

keyDecisions.decision: Deploy a dedicated EU-central-1 single-tenant sandbox instance for FinCorp's security validation audit.
keyDecisions.rationale: Satisfies Swiss financial market regulatory requirements for initial penetration testing.

keyDecisions.decision: Initiate a 45-day pilot with 100 wealth management advisors starting Dec 1.
keyDecisions.rationale: Proof of concept will measure time saved on client meeting documentation and compliance review speed.

actionItems.task: Send SOC 2 Type II report, ISO 27001 certificate, and standard BAA/DPA documents.
Provide architectural diagram showing Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) KMS encryption flow.
Review custom master services agreement (MSA) clauses with FinCorp legal counsel.

unresolvedQuestions.question: Does OmniNote AI support real-time redacting of PCI-DSS credit card and SSN identifiers from live audio?
unresolvedQuestions.context: Liam to demonstrate the automated PII masking engine during the sandbox onboarding session.

topics.summary: Claire highlighted that financial advisors currently spend 90 minutes each day manually writing meeting memorandums after client portfolio reviews.
Arthur verified that customer audio streams and text embeddings are never used to train base foundation models.
Agreed on 100-user pilot kickoff in December with weekly telemetry check-ins.

transcript.speaker: Sarah Jenkins
transcript.text: Arthur, Claire, thank you for joining us today. We're excited to explore how OmniNote can streamline meeting workflows for FinCorp's advisory teams.

transcript.speaker: Claire Dupont
transcript.text: Our primary problem is documentation overhead. Our 1,200 advisors are spending nearly two hours a day writing client notes. We need that automated, but compliance is strictly paramount.

transcript.speaker: Arthur Pendelton
transcript.text: Indeed. From a CISO standpoint, my red lines are simple: customer data must never be used to train foundation models, we need single-tenant VPC peering or dedicated cloud isolation, and our data must remain in Zurich or Frankfurt.

transcript.speaker: Liam O'Connor
transcript.text: We completely align with those requirements, Arthur. OmniNote offers zero data retention agreements. Furthermore, you can provision customer-managed KMS encryption keys so even our engineers have zero access to plaintext meeting transcripts.

transcript.speaker: Arthur Pendelton
transcript.text: That is reassuring. If you provide the KMS architecture specs and your latest SOC 2 Type II report, we can clear this for a 100-user pilot next month.

transcript.speaker: Sarah Jenkins
transcript.text: Fantastic. I'll dispatch the compliance bundle today, and Liam will send the encryption diagrams by Thursday. Thank you both!
